questions.q: The arithmetic mean of 4, 8, 6, 10 and 12 is
The median of the observations 7, 3, 9, 5, 11, 1 is
questions.e: Arranged in order the data are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. With six values, the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: (5 + 7)/2 = 6.

questions.q: For a moderately skewed distribution, Karl Pearson's empirical relation gives Mode = ______.
questions.e: The empirical relation is Mean − Mode = 3(Mean − Median), which rearranges to Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers is 7 is
questions.e: Six of the 36 equally likely outcomes give a sum of 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). So the probability is 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.q: A fair coin is tossed three times. The probability of getting at least one head is
questions.e: P(no head) = (1/2)³ = 1/8, so P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.q: The standard deviation of the data 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 (treated as a population) is
questions.e: The mean is 5. The squared deviations are 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16, which sum to 32. Variance = 32/8 = 4, so SD = √4 = 2.

questions.q: Which of the following can NOT be a value of Karl Pearson's coefficient of correlation?
questions.e: The correlation coefficient always lies between −1 and +1 inclusive. Therefore 1.25 is impossible.

questions.q: The mean of a binomial distribution with n = 20 and p = 0.25 is
questions.e: The mean of a binomial distribution is np = 20 × 0.25 = 5. The value 3.75 is the variance npq.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. For a Poisson distribution the mean and the variance are equal.
II. For a binomial distribution the mean is always equal to the variance.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: For Poisson both equal λ. For a binomial distribution the mean is np and the variance is npq, so they are equal only if q = 1, which is not possible when p > 0. Hence II is false.

questions.q: In a normal distribution, approximately what percentage of observations lie within one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.e: For a normal distribution about 68% of values lie within μ ± σ, 95% within μ ± 2σ and 99.7% within μ ± 3σ.

questions.q: Rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true is called a ______ error.
questions.e: Rejecting a true H₀ is a Type I error, whose probability is α. Accepting a false H₀ is a Type II error, whose probability is β.

questions.q: The two regression lines of y on x and of x on y always intersect at the point
questions.e: Both lines pass through the point of means (x̄, ȳ), because each is obtained by minimising squared deviations around the means.

questions.q: The mode of the data 3, 5, 5, 7, 5, 9, 7 is
questions.e: Mode is the most frequent value. 5 occurs three times, 7 twice and the rest once, so the mode is 5.

questions.q: If P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2, then P(A ∪ B) is
questions.e: By the addition rule, P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B) = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.7.

A fair coin is tossed 5 times. The probability of getting exactly 2 heads is
If X follows a Poisson distribution with mean 2, then P(X = 0) equals
questions.e: P(X = k) = e^(−λ) λᵏ / k!. For k = 0 and λ = 2 this gives e⁻² · 1/1 = e⁻².

questions.q: X is normally distributed with mean 50 and variance 16. The standard normal value (z-score) corresponding to X = 58 is
questions.e: The standard deviation is √16 = 4. So z = (X − μ)/σ = (58 − 50)/4 = 2. A common slip is dividing by the variance 16.

questions.q: If the correlation coefficient is 0.6, σₓ = 5 and σᵧ = 10, the regression coefficient of y on x is
questions.e: b(yx) = r · σᵧ/σₓ = 0.6 × 10/5 = 1.2. The regression coefficient of x on y would be r · σₓ/σᵧ = 0.3.

questions.q: A series has mean 30 and standard deviation 6. Its coefficient of variation is
A sample of size 100 from a population with σ = 10 has mean 50. Using z = 1.96, the 95% confidence interval for the population mean is
questions.e: The standard error is σ/√n = 10/10 = 1. The interval is 50 ± 1.96 × 1 = 48.04 to 51.96.

questions.q: The degrees of freedom for a chi-square test of independence on a 3 × 4 contingency table are
questions.e: Degrees of freedom = (rows − 1)(columns − 1) = (3 − 1)(4 − 1) = 6.

questions.q: A one-sample t-test is applied to a sample of size 15. The degrees of freedom are
questions.e: For a one-sample t-test the degrees of freedom are n − 1 = 15 − 1 = 14.

questions.q: The variance of a binomial distribution with n = 10 and p = 0.3 is
questions.e: Variance = npq = 10 × 0.3 × 0.7 = 2.1. The mean is np = 3.

questions.q: Three machines M₁, M₂ and M₃ produce 50%, 30% and 20% of the output of a plant, and their defect rates are 1%, 2% and 5% respectively. An item picked at random is found defective. The probability that it was produced by M₃ is
The regression lines of a bivariate data are 4x − 5y + 33 = 0 (y on x) and 20x − 9y = 107 (x on y). The correlation coefficient r is
questions.e: From the first line b(yx) = 4/5 and from the second b(xy) = 9/20. Then r² = (4/5)(9/20) = 9/25, so r = 0.6, positive because both coefficients are positive. The means are x̄ = 13 and ȳ = 17.

questions.q: A random variable X follows a Poisson distribution with mean 3. Then P(X ≤ 1) equals
questions.e: P(X = 0) = e⁻³ and P(X = 1) = 3e⁻³. Their sum is 4e⁻³.

questions.q: Group 1 has 40 items with mean 10 and variance 4. Group 2 has 60 items with mean 20 and variance 9. The variance of the combined 100 items is
questions.e: The combined mean is (400 + 1200)/100 = 16. Then variance = [40(4 + 6²) + 60(9 + 4²)]/100 = (1600 + 1500)/100 = 31. Averaging the two variances would ignore the gap between group means.

questions.q: A die is rolled 60 times and the faces 1 to 6 appear 5, 15, 10, 8, 12 and 10 times. For testing whether the die is fair, the value of the chi-square statistic is
questions.e: Each expected frequency is 60/6 = 10. χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E = (25 + 25 + 0 + 4 + 4 + 0)/10 = 58/10 = 5.8, with 5 degrees of freedom.
